card.name: Baishou Dance
card.profile: The Baishou Dance (摆手舞, baishouwu, 'hand-waving dance') is a group ritual dance of the Tujia people of Xiangxi, Hunan. Per English Wikipedia, 'It originates from an ancestor worship ceremony and dates back nearly 1,000 years ago, according to the broken stele in the Temple of Eight Clan Leaders (Qing Dynasty) and the county annals.' It uses 70 ritual gestures to represent war, farming, hunting, courtship and other aspects of traditional life, accompanied by gongs and drums. Per the Department of Culture and Tourism of Hunan Province, 'Grand Baishou is performed by over 1,000 dancers when offering sacrifices to the ancestors of the whole group.'
card.insight: It is one of China's oldest continuous folk dances and a key carrier of Tujia history, recognized as national intangible cultural heritage (Hunan provincial government).
